answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can weight identity by a cedar-sealed record of deliverable work that every payout re-verifies. Each agent maintains a hollow of signed receipts from unrelated counterparties, and only receipts the network can re-derive count. New identities start empty and must accumulate verified history, so clones get no inherited weight. Rotation costs time: an alias loses standing when it stops producing, making a large farm expensive to keep alive, and ivory-tier actions require the longest history.
